# Integration Requirements Checklist: Stable Planner and Configurable LLM Integration

**Purpose**: Review whether the Increment 012 requirements are complete, clear and measurable before implementation, with emphasis on deterministic authority, external-provider safety and product compatibility.
**Created**: 2026-11-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Deterministic Authority

- [ ] CHK001 Are the boundaries between interpretation, deterministic planning, explanation and shadow comparison explicitly defined without overlapping authority? [Completeness, Spec §Scope Decisions]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the prohibition on AI creating, modifying, approving or persisting alternatives consistent across scope, functional requirements and contracts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003–FR-004]
- [ ] CHK003 Are all deterministic gate families and the treatment of incomplete gate evidence specified precisely enough to prevent selectable partial plans? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Contract planner-adapter]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the stable behaviors to be ported enumerated while product-owned authentication, persistence and versioning boundaries are explicitly preserved? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-009]
- [ ] CHK005 Is “selective port” bounded by a named source commit and by explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria? [Traceability, Plan §Planner port boundary]

## Interpretation and Confirmation

- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements explicit that interpretation produces a proposal only and that user confirmation is required before values enter planning? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010–FR-013]
- [ ] CHK007 Are hard constraints, soft preferences, assumptions and unresolved fields defined consistently across spec, data model and API contract? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK008 Are unknown POIs, invalid values, prompt injection and semantically valid-but-wrong JSON covered by requirements? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the non-AI structured path defined as functionally complete rather than a reduced fallback? [Completeness, Spec §US3]

## Provider Configuration and Failure

- [ ] CHK010 Are provider, endpoint, model, credential, timeout, retry and capability configuration requirements complete without hard-coding one paid service? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK011 Are configuration, authentication, quota, safety, timeout, transport, malformed JSON and schema failures distinct and actionable? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK012 Are retry bounds and mutation/idempotency rules specified for late, repeated and concurrent provider responses? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018 and Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Is provider replacement explicitly required to preserve all product records and historical accepted plans? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, SC-007]
- [ ] CHK014 Are readiness requirements clear about what may be exposed and what secret/error detail must remain hidden? [Security, Spec §FR-020]

## Privacy and Grounding

- [ ] CHK015 Are external-processing disclosure and a non-AI choice required before sending traveler text to a hosted provider? [Privacy, Spec §FR-022–FR-023]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the minimum allowed provider payload defined well enough to exclude credentials, security data, audit records and unrelated private content? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK017 Are prompt/output retention defaults and allowed operational metadata consistent across requirements, data model and plan? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK018 Is explanation grounding objectively defined through valid evidence keys and deterministic fallback for unsupported claims? [Measurability, Spec §FR-025–FR-026, SC-006]
- [ ] CHK019 Are shadow privacy, anonymization, presentation-order checks and non-authoritative status specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027–FR-028]

## Product Compatibility and Verification

- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for preserving manual itinerary, map, route playback, expenses, offline reads and version history during the planner upgrade? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK021 Are one-day, two-day and unsupported longer-trip behaviors unambiguous and consistent across spec, contracts and mobile flow? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK022 Are historical and current regression obligations both required, rather than assuming the source branch’s measurements transfer automatically? [Completeness, Spec §FR-029–FR-031]
- [ ] CHK023 Are latency targets measurable and explicit about excluding optional shadow/explanation work? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK024 Are secret scanning, generated-artifact exclusions and real-key smoke-test boundaries specified? [Security, Spec §FR-032, SC-011]
- [ ] CHK025 Are mobile state labels and 390×844 requirements defined for AI success, AI failure, planner failure and offline state? [Coverage, Spec §SC-010, Contract mobile]

## Dependencies and Deferred Scope

- [ ] CHK026 Is the dependency on merging Increment 011 lifecycle fixes explicit before integrating planner changes? [Dependency, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK027 Is administration/data-operations work clearly deferred and protected from accidental inclusion? [Boundary, Spec §Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the distinction between a Gemini consumer subscription and Gemini Developer API key/quota documented for deployment? [Assumption, Research §Decision 4]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`.
